Event: `4ff4bc8b8ad21cba7ee3aad5872f4f7c` · 2026-09-24T20:18:12Z

> Red-team code review, checkpoint 1: ba154ca3f (model) and 7aedd10d6 (redoubt-stride). I used a scratch worktree at /tmp/k5-cr1 with its own target directory; it is removed now. The implementer's tree was not touched.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes. No P1. Four P2s, all test-strength or placement issues, to fix before or at commit 5.
> 
> RUN (release, host):
> - redoubt-stride: 9 unit tests plus the differential (3000 seeds x 400 steps) pass.
> - redoubt-model: all suites pass; mutations 120/120 detected; properties 6 (1 ignored); traces 4.
> - The crate builds for riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf.
> 
> RULES: the model implements every rule as approved.
> - Free weight = limit - carved (sched.rs:88).
> - Carve refusal: holds && weight == free && weight > 0 (kernel.rs budget_create). process_create is refused at free weight 0.
> - Fold at the old weight before a carve (add_budget) and before a return (destroy_budget), then rem rescaled and min(new-1).
> - The floor is monotone, raised at every fold, deschedule and reconcile, and held while the queue is empty.
> - Rank: wakes take front-1 in descending id; every runnable deschedule takes back+1; both reset when the queue empties.
> - Exact remainder charging, with the cap.
> - Entry e is stored. Lift = max(pass, f) + ((pass - max(e, f))+ x w_c + rem) / w_p, with the carry.
> - Boot is 1,000,000 / 250,000 / 749,000. Root keeps 1000 free and init stays in root; the boot check still passes.
> - Timeouts only wake; a budget deadline preempts; the equal-instant order is timeouts first.
> 
> MUTATIONS: each of the 19 is caught, and for a legitimate reason (the --nocapture output names the property). I also checked the intended scenario on its own, by seed residue. Detected:
> - gaming (d): DropRemainder (first at seed 1351) and ShortRunsFree (seed 21);
> - debt lift (i): UnnormalizedLift (seed 6);
> - churn (g): LiftByMax;
> - carve (h): StrideWeightIsLimit;
> - idempotence (l): FoldAtNewWeight;
> - sched_contracts: R7CarveToZeroFree and ProcessInWeightlessBudget (the free-weight invariant), TimeoutWakePreempts, PreemptOnWake, ExpireBudgetsFirst, BudgetDeadlineIgnored;
> - ipc_contracts: TimeoutIgnoredWhileOthersRun (I13).
> 
> DIFFERENTIAL: meaningful. The crate's rules are written independently of the model's (separate code; the queue is slot-based and the model is BTreeMap-based), and the comparison runs after every step on pass, entry, rem, tie, queued, floor, the counters and current. I planted 8 bugs in the crate (lift by max, ascending wake order, no rescale, requeue at the front, no floor raise at a fold, lift measured from f, no counter reset, rem dropped in the lift). The differential caught every one on the first failing seed.
> 
> DEBT-LIFT BOUND (K5-debt-lift-bound): the analysis is right. Equal-weight spinners sit at f or f + step, so S at f + epsilon ranks behind those at f and ahead of those at f + step, which is at most one round (N + 2 slices). R12UnnormalizedLift is caught decisively: S never runs within the 1000-slice cap (waited 10,000,000 µs against a bound of (n+3) x 10,000).
> 
> P2-1 The shell scenario (k) does NOT catch R12LiftCountsEntryWait: 0 of 3000 shell seeds (residue 9). Only idempotence (j) catches it. The shell's children are created when P usually has little lead, and the floor decays that lead between commands, so the geometric growth never appears. That matters for commit 5: the boot case sched-budget-churn (e) copies this shape. A kernel wiring bug that fails to persist entry (the frame word reading 0 makes the lift measure from f, which is exactly this mutation) would pass the boot bench. Strengthen (k), and the boot variant: have P create and destroy several heavy children back-to-back inside its own slice (tiny or no runs, P holding a lead). It should then fail under the mutation.
> 
> P2-2 Property (b) is vacuous in sched_rank. Every '_' iteration runs the slice to its end, so s.current is None whenever a wake (case 0) happens, and the 'a wake preempted' check never has a running thread. R12PreemptOnWake is caught only by sched_contracts' single timeout example (0 of 3000 rank seeds). Let wakes happen mid-slice: run part of a slice, wake, then check current is unchanged.
> 
> P2-3 DECISION 5's 'at least 1 tick per deschedule' is in neither the crate nor the model. charge() with runtime 0 charges nothing. Decide where it lives, the crate's fold or the kernel's trap-boundary accounting, and test it there. Otherwise a U-mode burst shorter than one tick (100 ns on QEMU's 10 MHz timebase) is free. If it goes in the crate, the model needs the matching floor (or the differential feeds max(1) to both).
> 
> P2-4 The differential's 'Kernel' is a harness written like the model (the same cursor, pending and deschedule code), not the kernel's future sched.rs. At commit 5, drive the kernel's actual wiring through this differential (e.g. put the wiring in a module both use), or it only proves crate = model.
> 
> P3:
> 1. lift: child.pass.saturating_sub(from) * w_child is an unchecked u128 multiply, and charge's rem + runtime x STRIDE assumes weight < 2^32 while the Budgets trait returns u64. Both are unreachable today, but checked builds would panic (I14). Use saturating_mul, and debug_assert or clamp weight <= u32::MAX.
> 2. Queue::reconcile loops forever if insert() finds no free slot (contains() stays false). That can't happen while runnable <= N, but a broken invariant would hang the kernel with SIE clear instead of failing. Break or assert when an insert fails.
> 3. The differential never destroys the running budget directly (its threads always exit first) and never a multi-level subtree in one operation (all threads ended, then bottom-up lifts with floor raises between). The kernel's deadline path does both; add those shapes.
> 4. DropRemainder is weakly caught by gaming (d) (only 1 of about 135 gaming seeds); the exact check in (l) carries it. That is fine, but (d)'s large-weight branch could burst smaller to bite more often.
